interpretation.acidic: Acidic soils may restrict phosphorus availability and micro-nutrients like molybdenum. Consider agricultural lime or dolomite if recommended by local soil testing.
interpretation.neutral: Near-neutral pH provides optimal availability of primary, secondary, and micronutrients for most field and horticultural crops.
interpretation.alkaline: Alkaline conditions can reduce the availability of phosphorus, iron, zinc, and manganese. Organic matter incorporation and gypsum may be evaluated based on local guidance.

nitrogen.name: Nitrogen (N)
nitrogen.description: Primary macronutrient for vegetative canopy and protein synthesis

interpretation.low: Available nitrogen is below standard agronomic sufficiency. Crops may show reduced vigor, pale leaves, and restricted vegetative growth.
interpretation.normal: Available nitrogen is in the recommended range supporting balanced vegetative growth and biomass development.
interpretation.high: Available nitrogen is abundant. Excessive nitrogen can cause succulent vegetative growth, delayed maturity, and increased susceptibility to pests.

phosphorus.name: Phosphorus (P)
phosphorus.description: Primary macronutrient for root establishment, energy transfer, and flowering

interpretation.low: Available phosphorus is deficient. Can restrict early seedling root branching and delay flowering and fruit setting.
interpretation.normal: Available phosphorus is at an adequate level supporting strong root architecture and timely reproductive development.
interpretation.high: Phosphorus levels are ample. High soil phosphorus reduces the need for heavy phosphatic inputs but requires monitoring for zinc uptake.

potassium.name: Potassium (K)
potassium.description: Primary macronutrient for water regulation, disease tolerance, and fruit quality

interpretation.low: Available potassium is deficient. Plants may exhibit marginal leaf scorching, weak stems, and reduced drought tolerance.
interpretation.normal: Available potassium is in the recommended range, providing good stomatal control, enzyme activation, and stress resistance.
interpretation.high: Available potassium is abundant, providing robust physiological resilience and quality crop yield.

organic_carbon.name: Organic Carbon (OC)
organic_carbon.description: Key indicator of biological activity, microbial biomass, and moisture retention

interpretation.low: Soil organic carbon is depleted. Soil may have low cation exchange capacity, poor moisture retention, and restricted microbial activity.
interpretation.normal: Soil organic carbon is moderate. Supports standard biological activity; regular addition of compost or green manure will sustain fertility.
interpretation.high: Soil organic carbon is favorable, fostering high biological diversity, excellent moisture buffering, and soil aggregation.

ec.name: Electrical Conductivity (EC)
ec.description: Indicator of soluble salt concentration and soil salinity hazards

interpretation.normal: Salinity levels are safe. Soluble salts will not cause osmotic stress to standard field and vegetable crops.
interpretation.medium: Mild salinity detected. Salt-sensitive crops may experience slight germination or osmotic delays; adequate drainage is advised.
interpretation.high: Elevated soil salinity. Significant osmotic stress may occur, reducing water uptake and root expansion. Salt-tolerant crops and flushing required.
